result.summary: The image depicts a standard urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and continuous sidewalks on both sides. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the environment lacks physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions to reduce crossing distances.

hazards.name: Pedestrian Exposure
hazards.description: The crossing distance across the main roadway is relatively wide without a refuge island, increasing the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic.

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Extensions
hazards.description: The absence of bulb-outs at the corners increases the crossing distance and may reduce visibility between pedestrians and turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to provide pedestrians with a 3-7 second head start before vehicles receive a green light.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Maintain and enhance the zebra markings to ensure they are highly visible to approaching motorists.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, continuous concrete sidewalk in good condition, bordered by a residential building and a large street tree. While the walkway is clear of obstructions, it lacks a physical buffer from the adjacent roadway and is characterized by a significant stretch of blank building frontage.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle separation
hazards.description: No physical buffer or bollards between the sidewalk and the travel lane.

hazards.name: Blank wall frontage
hazards.description: A large windowless wall reduces natural surveillance and 'eyes on the street'.
hazards.location_in_image: Ground floor of the yellow building

interventions.title: Street Furniture or Planters
interventions.description: Introduce a furniture zone with benches or planters to create a protective buffer between pedestrians and traffic.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and perceived safety for pedestrians at night.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban street with continuous sidewalks on both sides and buildings situated directly at the sidewalk edge. While the narrow geometry likely encourages lower vehicle speeds, the lack of marked crossings and the presence of parked cars on both sides create potential visibility hazards for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street can obscure pedestrians, particularly children, from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible street segment

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked crossing points visible on this block, forcing pedestrians to cross mid-block without priority or visibility aids.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers by moving the waiting area past the line of parked cars.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near potential crossing points to ensure clear sightlines for both pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, well-maintained sidewalk adjacent to a large institutional building. While the pedestrian walkway is clear and continuous, it lacks a physical buffer from the roadway and on-street parking, and no crossing infrastructure is visible in this mid-block section.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb can obscure pedestrians, particularly children, from the view of oncoming traffic if they attempt to cross the street mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line where the black vehicle is parked

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Install a furniture zone with street trees or planters to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.
